# preprocess.prepare_transcriptomic { #falconage.preprocess.prepare_transcriptomic }

```python
preprocess.prepare_transcriptomic(
    data,
    *,
    orthologues=None,
    genes=None,
    centre=True,
)
```

Run the whole chain, in order, recording each step.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Default   |
|-------------|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| orthologues | dict\[str, str\] \| pd.Series \| None | Source gene id to the model's gene id, for scoring one species with a model fitted in another. Applied first, and one-to-one only: a many-to-one map would silently sum paralogues into one column, and which paralogue a clock's coefficient refers to is not recoverable afterwards. | `None`    |
| genes       | list\[str\] \| None                   | The model's gene list. Absent genes are padded with NaN rather than dropped, so coverage reporting downstream sees them missing instead of never knowing they were expected.                                                                                                           | `None`    |
| centre      | bool                                  | The per-dataset median centring. ``False`` leaves it out, which is only right if you are going to do it yourself over the correct cohort.                                                                                                                                              | `True`    |
